applies_why: The judge text states that the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows were answered by [CR2] G, so it addresses whether cited verses are counted as unanswered witnesses under K-G4.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: The phrase 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it' could be read as either banning counting answered verses as unanswered witnesses or as still requiring a quote before any answer statement; I read it as banning the count, not requiring a quote when the judge treats the verse as answered.
why: The judge says the rows were answered by [CR2] G and does not count them as unanswered witnesses or toward a broken link, so it obeys K-G4.
